title: Pairwise maximin share allocations for three agents exist up to eight goods
description:
Unrefereed computer-assisted candidate. Every instance with three agents, nonnegative additive valuations and at most eight indivisible goods has a complete pairwise maximin share (PMMS) allocation; with the published nine-good counterexamples, nine is the least number of goods in a three-agent counterexample. A hypothetical eight-good counterexample is reduced by a written argument to ten propositional formulas, each refuted by a trimmed LRAT certificate; six- and seven-good existence is re-proved in the same framework. Every formula is re-derived clause by clause by a separate verifier, and every certificate is accepted by two LRAT checkers. The paper also proves a sufficient condition for PMMS with 3q-1 goods involving one balanced agent.

Files: the paper (pmms8.pdf); the core archive (generator, verifier, both checkers, all formulas and dictionaries, six- and seven-good certificates, receipts, replay script, manifest); and the ten eight-good certificates as separate files, those above 600 MB split into consecutive 400 MiB parts (.part00, .part01, ...); place_proofs.py joins them and puts them into the archive's layout after checking their SHA-256 digests.

Assurance: producer-side replay only. No formalisation in a proof assistant, independent reproduction, specialist review or editorial peer review. Historical priority is asserted only within a recorded literature search of 7-9 October 2026.
